stem: Which statement best describes a durable power of attorney for health care?

options.A: It authorizes an agent to manage only finances and property when the person cannot make decisions.
options.B: It names a health care proxy or agent to make health care decisions if the person cannot make or communicate those decisions, subject to the document and applicable state rules.
options.C: It functions as a do-not-resuscitate order and applies only to resuscitation decisions during cardiopulmonary arrest.
options.D: It transfers all health care decision-making authority to the agent immediately after signing, even while the person remains able to make and communicate decisions.

rationale: National Institute on Aging guidance describes a durable power of attorney for health care as an advance-directive document that names a health care proxy, representative, surrogate, or agent who can make health care decisions if the person is unable to make or communicate those decisions. The scope and formal requirements can vary by state and by the document. Therefore B is correct. A describes financial/property authority rather than the health care proxy role, C confuses the document with a DNR order, and D incorrectly displaces the decisions of a person who remains able to make and communicate health care choices.
educational_objective: Distinguish a durable power of attorney for health care from financial power of attorney and DNR orders: it names a health care agent to act when the person cannot make or communicate health care decisions, within the document and applicable state rules.
source_organization: National Institute on Aging (NIA), National Institutes of Health (NIH)

Choosing a Health Care Proxy > What is a health care proxy?: durable power of attorney for health care is the advance directive used to name the proxy; proxy acts when the person cannot make/communicate decisions; state requirements and permitted proxy responsibilities vary.

source_original.stem: Which statement best describes a durable power of attorney for health care?

options.A: The document authorizes an agent to manage only finances and property when the person cannot make decisions.
options.B: The document names an agent to make health care decisions if the person cannot decide or communicate, within applicable law.
options.C: The document functions as a DNR order and applies only to resuscitation decisions during cardiopulmonary arrest.
options.D: The document transfers all decision-making authority to the agent immediately after signing, even while the person remains capable.

source_original.rationale: A durable power of attorney for health care designates a proxy or agent to make health care decisions if the person becomes unable to decide or communicate, subject to the document and applicable state law. Option B is correct. It is distinct from financial authority and DNR orders, and it does not automatically displace a capable person's decisions.
source_original.source_detail: Durable power of attorney for health care section: names a health care proxy/agent to make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate or make decisions; state rules and document scope apply. correction_summary: Retained the advance-directive construct and key B. Tightened the correct option to distinguish inability to make/communicate health care decisions and explicitly preserved document/state-rule variability, avoiding unsupported universal claims about the agent's exact authority or activation standard.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only supported core functions and explicitly retains state/document variability. It does not claim a universal statutory activation process, specific proxy powers, or immediate transfer of authority while the person remains capable.

distractor_audit.A: Describes financial/property authority rather than the health care proxy role.
distractor_audit.C: A DNR order is distinct and narrower than a durable health care power of attorney.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly asserts immediate transfer of health care decision-making despite retained decision-making/communication ability.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B accurately identifies the document's health care proxy function and incapacity/communication context.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives define the document's function; no state-specific form name, threshold, or legal technicality cues the answer.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited NIA current guidance, state-law variability, all alternatives, rationale, objective, NCSBN advance-directive locator, ambiguity, cueing and legal precision. B remained uniquely correct.
